headline: Recommended a new Hale Street crosswalk, Common Lane safety signage, and approval of 46 Federal Street project
summary: The Commission recommended that the City Council support installing an ADA-compliant crosswalk on Hale Street near Oak and Juniper Streets, and support long-term sidewalk plans and interim signage for Common Lane. It also recommended that the Planning Board approve a site plan and special permit for a 5-unit townhouse project at 46 Federal Street, with conditions on parking, snow removal, and fire access. The Commission tabled approval of the January 6, 2026 minutes.
decisions: Recommended to City Council that the Commission supports installing a crosswalk crossing Hale Street near Oak Street and Juniper Street, at an ADA-compliant location with a sidewalk connection; motion carried by roll call 5-0.
Recommended sending a letter to City Council supporting long-term sidewalk plans for Common Lane and suggesting 'Share the Road' signage in the meantime; motion carried by roll call 5-0.

Recommended that the Planning Board approve Site Plan Review application #170-26 (SPR-26-2) and Special Permit application #205-26 (SP-26-6) for 46 Federal Street with four listed conditions; motion carried 5-0.
Tabled review of the January 6, 2026 meeting minutes to the next meeting.

2. Recommendation to City Council: Order #26-059 – Request that the Parking & 20 
Traffic Commission review the decision to remove the crosswalk at the interior of 21 
Hale Street and Juniper Street in Beverly Farms – Matthew St. Hilaire, Ward 6 City 22 
Councilor. 23 
 24 
Ward 6 City Councilor Matthew St. Hilaire explained that he previously worked with 25 
Commissioner Collins and the Mayor to repave Hale Street down to West Beach. There was a 26 
crosswalk for 30 years that served residents in this area as a connection point to the Hastings 27 
House, MBTA train station, Beverly Farms Business District, etc. It cut across Hale Street from 28 
Juniper Street and there is not another crosswalk close by. This is also a major thoroughfare 29 
through Beverly Farms and served as a safety net for many in the neighborhood. He has heard 30 
from residents that they miss this connection and feel that it is an important safety feature. 31 
 32 
Benevento stated that crosswalks have to be ADA compliant. There also needs to be a logical 33 
beginning and end for a crosswalk. This one appears to run to an area of grass which would not 34 
be compliant. Per the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD), crosswalks should 35 
not be used indiscriminately and should be part of an engineering study. It does not matter that 36 
there was previously a sidewalk in this area for 30 years. It does seem that residents believe a 37 
crosswalk is needed, but there needs to be consideration as to where it should appropriately be 38 
placed. There would also need to be consideration of funding for this, especially as the road was 39 
recently rebuilt.  40 
 41 
Collins stated that ramps would have to be built on both sides in order to make the crosswalk 42 
ADA compliant.  43
